title: Amputation and ostomy status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM status codes this note supports.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for hypertension and joint pain.

HPI
Pt is an 80 y.o. female presenting for a routine follow-up of chronic hypertension and osteoarthritis of the hands. Pt reports mild aching in bilateral MCP and PIP joints, worse in the morning. Denies any acute swelling or redness. Pt has a history of a left above-knee amputation several years ago. She currently uses a prosthesis for mobility. She reports that her blood pressure has been stable at home with current meds. Denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or syncope.

Medication List
Lisinopril 20mg daily
Amlodipine 5mg daily
Acetaminophen 650mg BID PRN for joint pain

Review of Systems
Constitutional: No fever, chills, or weight changes.
HEENT: No vision changes, no headaches.
Respiratory: No SOB, no cough.
Musculoskeletal: Bilateral hand joint pain, no acute injuries.
Skin: No rashes.
Neurological: No numbness or weakness.

Social History
Retired. Lives with her daughter. Independent in ADLs. Non-smoker.

Family History
Mother: Hypertension, Stroke.
Father: Myocardial Infarction.

Vitals
BP: 132/82
HR: 74 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 97% on RA
Ht/Wt: 145 lbs

Recent Labs
BMP: Na 139, K 4.2, BUN 18, Cr 1.0, eGFR 82.
HbA1c: 5.6%

Exam
General: Alert, oriented x3, in no acute distress.
Cardiovascular: RRR, regular S1/S2, no murmurs.
Respiratory: CTAB.
Musculoskeletal: Left above-knee amputation site is well-healed with no drainage or erythema. Hand joints show mild non-inflammatory swelling.
Neurological: Grossly intact.

Assessment
1. Hypertension: Well-controlled on current regimen.
2. Osteoarthritis: Hand joints.
3. Left AKA: Stable status.

Plan
1. Continue Lisinopril and Amlodipine as prescribed.
2. Continue Acetaminophen PRN for hand pain.
3. Follow up in 3 months for routine BP check.

Electronically signed, T. Haddad, NP, 05/14/2026
explanations: Acquired absence of the left leg above the knee: Z89.612 (HCC 409).

distractors.why: The amputation status is documented and still applies.
The amputation is above the knee.
